# comment: AI-READI clinical_data/measurement.csv items mapped to HPO. EVERY ROW IS A MEASURED-VALUE MAPPING (evidence_code ECO:0007307, direct assay evidence used in automatic assertion) - the subject is an assay, the object a phenotype, and the phenotype is entailed only when the value falls outside a reference range, which is what the when_value gate encodes. The term-to-term predicate is therefore skos:relatedMatch throughout - an assay is not the phenotype - and the gate is what makes the row derive anything. ABSENT POLES ARE ASSERTED HERE, unlike the self-report sets - a normal result on a dated assay rules the abnormality out at that observation, and the derived feature carries the measurement's own time, which is what qualifies the exclusion (predicate_modifier Not; see docs/mapping-conventions.md 'Measured-value mappings'). Subjects are b2ai:measurement.<redcap_variable>, matching config/aireadi/measurement, never the concept id (3004249 backs both blood-pressure readings). THRESHOLDS, in order of preference - (1) the performing lab's published interval, UW NORC, as reproduced at docs.aireadi.org v3 clinical-lab-tests, for the import_* central-lab analytes; (2) ABIM Laboratory Test Reference Ranges (January 2025) for the site-lab CBC (lbscat_*), which AI-READI publishes no interval for; (3) guideline categories where the phenotype is category-defined (ACC/AHA 2017 blood pressure, NCEP ATP III lipids, ADA glycemia, WHO waist/WHR and BMI, ICD-11 vision impairment); each row names its source in threshold_source. The per-row range_low/range_high columns are NOT read - they are null-as-zero on every row seen in the public release. SEX-BLIND GATES - Individual.sex is redacted in the public release, so for a sex-split interval the present pole fires only where abnormal for both sexes and the absent pole only where normal for both; the band between asserts nothing (marked per row). loinc2hpo supplied the candidate term for most central-lab analytes (loinc_id + l2h_outcome record which); four of its targets were overridden and are documented in place - an obsolete term (718-7 H), a wrong analyte (30522-7 L, 4548-4 L, 2161-8 H), and pCO2 terms for a serum bicarbonate assay (2028-9). PER-EYE AND PER-FOOT items assert presence from either side and carry no absent pole, because a normal side cannot rule out the fellow side. NOT MAPPED, and why - lbscat_mchc (HPO's MCHC terms are defined as MCH, see lbscat_mch); import_a_g_ratio and import_buncreatinineratio (no HPO term; the components are mapped); import_urine_creatinine (a normaliser, and loinc2hpo's target is the serum term); height, weight and hip circumference alone (captured by BMI and WHR); mesopic acuity and contrast sensitivity (no low-luminance term in HPO); letter-count, miss-count and axis columns (inputs to the derived scores); the MoCA sub-item scores and every *_time column (no score-defined HPO terms). Confidence 0.9 = performing-lab interval, sex-agnostic; 0.85 = guideline category or sex-blind conservative band; 0.8 = age/sex-stratified table collapsed to its extremes, or an ADA/lab compromise; 0.6-0.75 = a stated approximation (unit unresolved, concentration standing in for a ratio, sphere for spherical equivalent).
